notes: The test plots the terrain's look is perfected on (roadmap L1, docs/scenery/TERRAIN_ROADMAP.md part A; the catalogue in docs/research/TERRAIN_PROCEDURAL_METHOD_2026-11.md section 6.2). Each is found on the map by its anchor, as the views are (data/scenery/views.json), and rendered at the plot lab's fixed exposure, 0 EV unless its exposure_ev says otherwise (tools/plot_lab.py, A.3.20), and seen from three cameras looking at its middle: eye (1.7 m, 30 m back), low (25 m, 43 m back) and high (150 m, 260 m back) (simcore/scenery/plots.hpp). A field_layer anchor finds the nearest field within 3 km of close_km whose whole 50 m square is one parcel in that ground layer on the scenario's day (with edge set true, the cameras look at where that field ends toward them, from outside it: a standing crop's face); turn_deg turns the cameras from the anchor's own bearing (a field's: its furrows). Close to battery 21's district (10 m ground) where it can be. Photos are ids in views.json's register. Rendered by -SimMapShots=<folder> -SimShotSet=plots, set beside their photographs and their last approved render by tools/plot_lab.py. Presentation only.

plots.name: Ploughland (autumn)
plots.must_see: Furrows along the parcel's heading at the plough's 30-50 cm, big dry clods, a pale dusty top; the headland worked across the furrows; the parcel's edge against its neighbour.

plots.name: Maize stover (harvested)
plots.must_see: Stalks lying and broken, stumps in rows 70-76 cm apart, cut stalks or bales in places.

plots.name: Standing maize (dry)
plots.must_see: A 2-3 m wall of dry tan stalks in rows; the field's edge as a face.

plots.name: Standing sunflower (dry)
plots.must_see: A 1.6-2 m stand of near-black dry stalks in rows, the heads hanging face down; darker than maize from afar.

plots.name: Wheat stubble
plots.must_see: Short straw 10-20 cm in the drill's rows, the combine's straw lines, weeds.

plots.name: Inside a black locust wood on the plain
plots.must_see: Dense thin stems, many in groups from one stool, 12-20 m; open light crowns of small leaflets turning yellow, light reaching the floor; elder under them (method 6.2 row 8). Never a wall.

plots.name: Inside a hybrid poplar plantation by the water
plots.must_see: Straight grey boles in a strict 6 x 6 m lattice, one age, lanes running away between the rows; the crowns high and narrow, gold; grass or bare ground between (method 6.2 row 9).

plots.name: Forest edge against a field
plots.must_see: The herb fringe, a shrub belt, a mantle of lower trees, then the stand; never a wall.

plots.name: Road with verge and ditch
plots.must_see: Asphalt 4-6 m, earth shoulders 1-2 m, a ditch, a pole line, a tree row on one side.

plots.name: River bank with reeds
plots.must_see: A reed belt 1-5 m wide, reeds 2-4 m tall, willows on the bank.

plots.name: Village ground
plots.must_see: The town's open ground (the yard layer): packed earth and gravel worn by wheels, weeds at the edges.

plots.name: The battery's position, worn
plots.must_see: Ground churned by the vehicles: wheel ruts in mud, bare earth, the grass left only between.

plots.name: A field's edge on a slope in the hill country
plots.must_see: The field climbing the slope, its edge and the hill beyond; the ground rolling, not flat (look target K1, K3).

plots.name: A wood's edge on a hillside
plots.must_see: The wood holding the slope, its edge layered and closed; the ground falling away (look target K2, K4).

plots.name: Alders along a brook in the hills
plots.must_see: A line of dark alders on one bank of a narrow brook in a valley floor, broken in places; meadow to the water.

plots.name: Inside a wood in the hills
plots.must_see: Trunks receding into shade, the crowns closed overhead, hazel and elder in patches under them, the floor dark; never a wall or a green slab (A.3.19, A.3.21).

plots.name: A village pond in the hills
plots.must_see: Still water low in its hollow at the village's edge, a soft grassed bank rising from it, reeds along the water, a waterside tree; the village behind (the look target's K-f).

plots.name: A sunken lane up a loess slope
plots.must_see: A track worn 1-5 m into the slope between grassed banks, deepest halfway up, shrubs and trees along the banks' tops, the field beyond hidden (A.3.34).

plots.name: Tall grass in the hills, left unmown
plots.must_see: Grass knee-high and gone to seed, pale and dry in October, uneven in tussocks; the hay meadow and pasture beside it mown and grazed short (terrain roadmap L13, A.3.39).
